source.title: Towards Multimodal Interpretability: Learning Sparse Interpretable Features in Vision Transformers

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse-autoencoder feature analysis to a CLIP vision transformer and reports results in this new setting. It does not test the claim versions that specifically concern toy networks or LLMs.
record.gate_note: The post measures SAE sparsity, feature-cluster properties, and alignment between SAE features and MLP neurons. It does not test whether features compete for capacity, whether feature importance determines geometry, or whether SAE features are stable and complete canonical units. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The post trains an SAE on CLIP ViT-L's residual stream. It reports sparse, interpretable recovered features and polysemantic MLP neurons. That bears on V4 in a new setting: a vision transformer rather than an LLM. It does not test toy models, capacity, stability or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that SAEs find sparse, highly interpretable directions in the residual stream of a CLIP vision transformer. Many features are not neuron-aligned, and inspected MLP neurons look polysemantic. The author attributes limitations, including the large ultra-low-density cluster and the odd drop in loss, to training on ImageNet-1k, and calls for replication on a larger dataset.
record.recipe_differences: This post trains an SAE on the residual stream of a CLIP vision transformer and analyzes its features; it does not report a toy-network test. The original method is not described in the post.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-distribution analysis is described for expansion factors 64 and 16; the author says the results are very similar. Training dataset is ImageNet-1k.

fits_no_version.finding: Most SAE features fall in an ultra-low-density cluster whose encoder vectors are highly similar. One image activated 6458 features (39.42%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on vision transformers trained on narrow datasets produce a large redundant cluster representing a single direction.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features show no alignment with earlier-layer MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer residual SAE features in a ViT are not aligned with earlier MLP output vectors.

record.problems: The analysis uses ImageNet-1k, which the author says is not very high-dimensional or particularly sparse and differs from CLIP's internet-scale training data. The author reports 86% explained variance and says further investigation is needed. Several feature interpretations are illustrated with a small selected subset; neuron-alignment results are described as crude, with some results approximate or lacking numerical detail. Only one named model is studied.

untested.parts: LLMs specifically; only a vision transformer (CLIP ViT-L) is studied.
No toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
Capacity competition and importance-based allocation are not tested.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity are not tested.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. The redundant ultra-low-density cluster is suggestive but not analysed for this question.
One-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features is not tested.

missing.what: Reconstruction quality: explained variance 86% and MSE 0.0027. The contrastive loss with the SAE inserted (1.775) is lower than the original model's (1.895).
missing.locator: MSE, l1 and Model Losses table

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked the study as tests/T3 but linked no versions, which is inconsistent. I linked V4 on the basis that a ViT is a new setting for V4's 'real models' claim, while noting the LLM restriction as untested. This is a LessWrong post with one model, one layer and qualitative neuron inspection.

versions.untested_parts: Tests neither toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions nor a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
Reports polysemantic MLP neurons but does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dimension sharing.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Studies a vision encoder, not an LLM; does not test the version's LLM-specific claim.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT Large
rows.operation_detail: Compared each non-ultra-low-frequency SAE encoder vector with MLP output vectors and took its maximum cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Maximum cosine similarity to an MLP output vector
rows.value: Approximately half of SAE features are above the random-vector range; approximately half are within or below it.
rows.note: The post gives approximate proportions, not exact counts.
rows.check: Linked to V4. About half of the SAE features are more neuron-aligned than random, so features are not uniformly spread across neurons.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure alone. Approximately half exceed the random-vector maximum-cosine range [0.08, 0.14]; approximately half are within or below it. This does not establish incomplete sparse-feature recovery or measure distribution across many neurons.
source_check.problem: The partial state interprets a cosine-alignment diagnostic as incomplete V4; V4 does not require all features to be neuron-unaligned.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT Large
rows.operation_detail: Counted MLP neurons with cosine similarity above the post's neuron-alignment threshold for each SAE feature.
rows.measure: Number of aligned MLP neurons per SAE feature
rows.value: About half of features are not neuron aligned; the other half are aligned mostly to fewer than 5 MLP neurons.
rows.note: The author calls this a crude analysis.
rows.check: Linked to V4. About half of the features are not neuron-aligned; the rest align to a few (<5) MLP neurons. This is consistent with distribution across neurons only for part of the features.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure alone. At cosine similarity >0.14, about half have no aligned MLP neurons; the remainder align mostly to fewer than 5. The author describes this analysis as crude.
source_check.problem: Counting thresholded alignments does not establish that V4 holds only partially; sparse dictionary recovery is compatible with alignment to a few neurons.

rows.subject: CLIP ViT Large
rows.operation_detail: Inspected highest-activating images for each MLP neuron.
rows.measure: Polysemanticity of MLP neurons in highest-activating images
rows.value: The author reports that all inspected MLP neurons appeared to combine typically 3 or 4 unrelated data features and were less interpretable than the SAE features.
rows.note: The number of neurons inspected is not stated.
rows.check: Linked to V4. MLP neurons appear polysemantic, mixing 3–4 unrelated features. The evidence is qualitative and the number of neurons inspected is not stated.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure alone. All inspected MLP neurons appeared polysemantic, typically combining 3 or 4 unrelated features, and were much less interpretable than SAE features. Inspection count is not stated.
source_check.problem: Neuron polysemanticity alone establishes neither feature distribution across many neurons nor sparse dictionary recovery.

relationships.condition: Same setting; neuron alignment and reconstruction quality

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Same setting; neuron alignment and reconstruction quality
source_check.reason: R6 and R8 do not contradict V4's sparse-recovery alternative or its non-universal distribution claim. Explained variance of 86% and a degenerate ultra-low-density cluster qualify dictionary quality; V4 does not require complete reconstruction or every latent to be useful. These diagnostics do not establish a separate condition where V4 fails or needs narrowing.

relation.reason: Reports its own sparse-feature recovery and interpretability analyses, bearing on V4 beyond merely using an SAE as a tool.

tranche.reason: Tests sparse interpretable dictionary recovery in a new real-model setting: the vision encoder of multimodal CLIP.

source_check.notes: V4 support is an extension to CLIP's vision encoder, not a direct LLM result. Interpretability evidence is qualitative; the author treats ImageNet-related explanations as tentative and calls for replication on a larger dataset.

statements.correction: CLIP ViT-L layer-22 class-token residual stream; non-ultra-low-frequency features only; alignment threshold cosine >0.14; about half align mostly to fewer than 5 MLP neurons; about half have no aligned neurons; inspected MLP neurons qualitatively much less interpretable than SAE features.
statements.problem: The CLIP proportion and alignment condition are correct, but their placement as evidence narrowing SAE advantages overstates this diagnostic. Alignment does not establish comparable neuron interpretability; the author reports substantially less interpretable MLP neurons.
